findings.claim: Real gyroscopes have constant bias and white rate noise with the declared densities

hypothesis: Integrating a gyro with constant bias b and white rate noise of density N gives heading error with mean b t and variance N^2 t; in 3-D the bias error rotates with the body, so transverse bias stays bounded while the random walk stays isotropic.
mathematical_model: Single axis: e(t) = b t + N W(t). Strapdown: E_{k+1} = exp(-[w] dt) E_k exp([w + b + n] dt); linearized e_{k+1} = exp(-[w] dt) e_k + J_r(w dt)(b + n) dt, so transverse components circle with radius |b_perp|/|w| (maximum 2|b_perp|/|w|).
numerical_result: single-axis max |z| = 1.35; rotating transverse max 6.365e-04 rad vs bound 6.366e-04 (stationary 1.000e-02); linearization error 3.2e-04.
observation_model: Synthetic imu_orientation outputs from integrated gyro rates; no accelerometer or magnetometer aiding.

physical_validation_status.statement: Physical validation requires acquired hardware evidence; none was acquired for this task.
